The binary drives 9 subtests (memfd_create01.c:220-232), each creating a fresh memfd of MFD_DEF_SIZE=8192 named ltp_memfd_create01 and asserting the correct kernel's per-call returns: (1) Basic tests + set/get seals -- F_GET_SEALS on a fresh MFD_ALLOW_SEALING fd returns 0; F_ADD_SEALS of SHRINK|WRITE then re-adding the same is idempotent; adding GROW|SEAL yields the union 0xF; any later F_ADD_SEALS, including seals==0, returns EPERM. (2) Disabled sealing -- a memfd created with flags 0 reports F_SEAL_SEAL (0x1) already set and every F_ADD_SEALS returns EPERM. (3) Write seal -- after F_SEAL_WRITE the fd stays readable, write() returns EPERM, ftruncate down/up still succeed, and a growing write returns EPERM. (4) Shrink seal -- reads/writes succeed, ftruncate below current size returns EPERM, growth via ftruncate and via write both succeed. (5) Grow seal -- ftruncate above size returns EPERM, ftruncate down succeeds, growing write returns EPERM. (6) Resize seal (SHRINK|GROW) -- both ftruncate directions return EPERM while in-place read/write succeed. (7) Seals shared for dup -- seals live on the inode, not the fd: adding via fd is visible through dup'd fd2 and vice versa, and after F_SEAL_SEAL both fds return EPERM, including after fd2 is closed. (8) Seals shared for mmap -- with a live MAP_SHARED PROT_WRITE mapping, F_ADD_SEALS(F_SEAL_WRITE) returns EBUSY and leaves seals unchanged at 0, while F_SEAL_SHRINK still succeeds; after munmap and a MAP_PRIVATE PROT_READ mapping, F_SEAL_WRITE succeeds. (9) Seals shared for open -- open(/proc/self/fd/N, O_RDWR) gives a separate file context sharing the same seals both directions; an O_RDONLY reopen returns EPERM on F_ADD_SEALS while F_GET_SEALS still reads correctly; and once F_SEAL_WRITE is set, open(/proc/self/fd/N, O_RDWR|O_CREAT) returns EPERM.
failing_assertion: None. Asterinas passes all 157 assertions with 0 failed / 0 broken / 0 skipped, identical to the host baseline.
root_cause: Not applicable -- no defect. The pool entry is stale: test/initramfs/src/conformance/ltp/testcases/all.txt line 1879 still carries the commented-out `# memfd_create01`, so the test is never packaged into the initramfs and CI has never observed that it passes. Asterinas grew a full memfd implementation (kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/ramfs/memfd.rs) with a dedicated MemfdInode carrying a Mutex<FileSeals>, and every assertion the test makes is covered there: add_seals rejects on F_SEAL_SEAL with EPERM (lines 50-52) and unions new seals into the existing set (line 69), so idempotent re-adds and the 0xF union both behave; new_memfd pre-seeds F_SEAL_SEAL when MFD_ALLOW_SEALING is absent (lines 257-260), which is what makes subtest 2 pass; the seals Mutex lives on the inode rather than the handle, so dup and the /proc/self/fd reopen in subtests 7 and 9 observe one shared set; add_seals on the handle returns EPERM when Rights::WRITE is absent (lines 282-284), covering the O_RDONLY reopen; page_cache().writable_mapping_status().deny() (lines 64-67) is what produces EBUSY under a live writable mapping in subtest 8; resize enforces SHRINK and GROW in both directions (lines 178-189); and write_at rejects sealed writes and implements Linux's EOF-page granularity for F_SEAL_GROW (lines 107-146), which is what the growable-by-write assertions in subtests 3-6 distinguish.
invariant: A conformance test that passes must not remain excluded from the packaged suite -- a commented-out entry in all.txt asserts the test still fails, so leaving it commented lets the behavior it covers regress silently.
linux_reference: Not needed for a fix, but the implementation already tracks it: memfd.rs cites mm/memfd.c (F_SEAL_EXEC implying SHRINK|GROW|WRITE|FUTURE_WRITE at v6.16.5 L262-266, and the MAY_WRITE downgrade at L356), mm/shmem.c L3309-3310 for the F_SEAL_GROW EOF-page write behavior, and mm/shmem.c L3828-3850 for the internal memfd tmpfs mount. Linux keeps seals on the inode (shmem_inode_info->seals), which is the same placement Asterinas chose.

reproduction.note: The LTP runner in this suite suppresses per-assertion TPASS lines in qemu.log and prints only the aggregate, so the assertion-level comparison rests on the passed count matching exactly. 157 is the exact host figure, and it is load-bearing: memfd_create01.c:258-261 tst_brk(TCONF)s the whole binary if MFD_ALLOW_SEALING is unavailable, so an unimplemented seal path would show skipped>0 and a passed count far below 157 rather than a silent partial run.
